videos.script: In lesson 3, a device refused a prefix length of thirty-three. Nobody wrote that rule into the device. It came from one line in a file. {{refused}} That file is a YANG model. It says what the configuration looks like: which items exist, how they nest, and which values are allowed. {{model}} NETCONF, RESTCONF and gNMI all carry data shaped by models like it. That is why the same description could be written one way and read another. {{same}} In this lesson you read models as trees, and learn the few symbols that make them readable. You see one model extend another, and two groups draw the same interface in different ways. {{trees}} Then you write a small model of your own, for the lab's branches, and check data against it. Four mistakes, four refusals, each one pointing at the line that caught it. {{write}} Last, you ask a device which models it has, because it can only hold data for those. {{device}}
